literature.headline_zh: 马尔堡病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期马尔堡病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 结果多维分子分析显示 MARV 和哺乳动物群体之间存在不同的基因组相似性,在奇蹄目和某些啮齿动物中观察到多个密码子使用指数的稳定收敛。值得注意的是,马属马 (Equus caballus) 的有效密码子数 (ENC) (52.43) 几乎与 MARV (52.44) 相当,而马马 (Equus asinus) 与病毒的平均 RSCU 曼哈顿距离最低 (0.25)。此外,MARV 的 CpG 抑制 ($$\:{\rho\:}_{CpG}$$ = 0.48) 与所研究的哺乳动物类群的 CpG 消耗水平特征一致。 [10.1186/s12864-026-13256-y]
审查得出的结论是,马尔堡病毒病 (MVD) 是一种由 马尔堡病毒 引起的高致死性人畜共患出血热。它综合了 MVD 的当前证据,涵盖 流行病学、发病机制、诊断和新兴对策,例如研究性 抗病毒药物 和 疫苗。分子病毒学的进步有助于阐明免疫逃避和病毒持续存在的机制,为有针对性的干预策略提供信息。 [10.1007/s44370-026-00055-y]
研究发现,对于 马尔堡病毒,人类活动和行为、土地覆盖和 宿主 密度被视为关键风险因素,而对于 马尔堡病毒病,观察到基于专家的风险因素和基于文献的风险因素之间存在趋同和分歧,特别是在牲畜贸易和社会文化实践方面。 [10.1186/s42522-026-00232-5]
与 FILMARRAY 2.0 相比,BioThreat Panel v2.5 对所有目标在 SPOTFIRE 上表现出同等或更好的灵敏度,但鼠疫耶尔森氏菌除外,由于 SPOTFIRE 上的调用方案经过修改,鼠疫杆菌显示出灵敏度降低。 [10.1007/s44340-026-00058-x]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Results Multidimensional molecular profiling showed varied genomic similarity between MARV and mammalian groups, with stable convergence observed in Perissodactyla and certain rodents across multiple codon usage indices. [10.1186/s12864-026-13256-y]

The review concludes that Marburg virus disease (MVD) is a highly lethal zoonotic haemorrhagic fever caused by the Marburg virus. It synthesises current evidence on MVD, covering epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnostics, and emerging countermeasures, such as investigational antivirals and vaccines. [10.1007/s44370-026-00055-y]

The study found that for Marburg virus, human activities and behaviours, land cover, and host density were perceived as critical risk factors, while for Marburg virus disease, convergences and divergences were observed between expert-based and literature-based risk factors, particularly concerning livestock trade and socio-cultural practices. [10.1186/s42522-026-00232-5]

The BioThreat Panel v2.5 exhibited equivalent or better sensitivity on SPOTFIRE compared to FILMARRAY 2.0 for all targets, except for Yersinia pestis, which displayed reduced sensitivity due to a modified calling scheme on SPOTFIRE. [10.1007/s44340-026-00058-x]

news.headline_zh: 马尔堡病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期马尔堡病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 埃塞俄比亚将出席世界卫生组织非洲区域委员会第七十六届会议,该委员会是世界卫生组织非洲区域办事处的理事机构。该活动已确认为计划中的会议。 [news-692e217b26e11ef6]
Public Health 疫苗 (PHV) 获得 BioMaP 联盟授予的一份合同,将其 PHV01、rVSV-MARV 疫苗 的生产和测试技术转让给美国设施。 [news-45a1823079189963]
Island Pharmaceuticals 收到 FDA 确认,动物规则途径适合开发加利地韦作为针对 马尔堡病毒 的对策,并且加利地韦在批准后将有资格获得热带病优先审查券。 [news-12e06be226dcdcc1]
由世界卫生组织 (WHO) 赞助,在刚果启动了一项实验性埃博拉试验,以测试 治疗 的 Bundibugyo 毒株。该试验包括单克隆抗体混合物 MBP134 和 抗病毒药物 瑞德西韦以及优化的支持护理。这是根据世界卫生组织的公告确认的事件。 [news-3bc29e26561ca538]
HOPE 项目正在监测埃博拉病毒 暴发 并为当地合作伙伴提供医疗用品。暴发 是由该病毒的 Bundibugyo 毒株引起的,这是该病毒的一种罕见形式。2026年5月15日,世界卫生组织(WHO)确认暴发为国际关注的突发公共卫生事件。 [news-5bfc99ae64074acb]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Marburg virus news developments.
key_findings_en: Ethiopia will host the Seventy-sixth Session of the WHO Regional Committee for Africa, which is the governing body of the WHO Regional Office for Africa. This event is confirmed as a planned meeting. [news-692e217b26e11ef6]
Public Health Vaccines (PHV) was awarded a contract by the BioMaP-Consortium to tech transfer production and testing of its PHV01, rVSV-MARV vaccine to U.S.-based facilities. [news-45a1823079189963]

Island Pharmaceuticals received FDA confirmation that the Animal Rule pathway is appropriate for developing galidesivir as a countermeasure against Marburg virus, and that galidesivir would qualify for a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher upon approval. [news-12e06be226dcdcc1]

An experimental Ebola trial was launched in Congo, sponsored by the World Health Organization (WHO), to test treatments for the Bundibugyo strain. The trial includes monoclonal antibody cocktail MBP134 and antiviral remdesivir alongside optimized supportive care. This is a confirmed event based on the WHO's announcement. [news-3bc29e26561ca538]

Project HOPE is monitoring the Ebola outbreak and connecting local partners with medical supplies. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, which is a rare form of the virus. [news-5bfc99ae64074acb]

papers.title: Divergent host adaptation in Marburg virus: a hypothesis-generating framework for prioritizing non-traditional reservoirs
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Although Rousettus aegyptiacus is the primary natural reservoir of Marburg virus (MARV), recent atypical outbreaks and viral genomic diversification suggest a highly complex host-pathogen ecology. Here, we systematically evaluated the molecular homologies between MARV and diverse mammalian taxa to identify putative reservoir hosts and guide targeted surveillance. Methods A multi-dimensional molecular characterization of the Marburg virus (MARV) genome was performed using an integrative suite of computational approaches. Distant sequence homology was interrogated via BLAST in conjunction with a null model framework, supplemented by granular analyses of codon usage bias, nucleotide composition, and dinucleotide frequencies. For comparative genomic context, we evaluated a cohort of 63 mammalian species across the orders Rodentia, Primates, Chiroptera, and Perissodactyla. Results Multidimensional molecular profiling showed varied genomic similarity between MARV and mammalian groups, with stable convergence observed in Perissodactyla and certain rodents across multiple codon usage indices. Notably, the effective number of codons (ENC) in Equus caballus (52.43) nearly matched MARV (52.44), and Equus asinus exhibited the lowest average RSCU Manhattan distance to the virus (0.25). Additionally, MARV’s CpG suppression ( $$\:{\rho\:}_{CpG}$$ = 0.48) was consistent with the CpG depletion levels characteristic of the studied mammalian taxa. Conclusion Through the lens of computational biology, this study identifies putative host cohorts within the orders Perissodactyla and Rodentia that share distinct genomic, codon-usage, and dinucleotide-frequency homologies with MARV. These findings establish high-priority targets for downstream ecological field monitoring, seroepidemiological surveys, and experimental validation, ultimately providing a scientific blueprint to refine zoonotic surveillance networks under the global ‘One Health’ paradigm.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 摘要 背景 虽然 Rousettus aegyptiacus 是 马尔堡病毒 (MARV) 的主要天然 马尔堡病毒,但最近的非典型 暴发 和病毒基因组多样化表明 宿主 病原体生态学高度复杂。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 为了比较基因组背景,我们评估了啮齿目、灵长目、翼手目和奇蹄目 63 个哺乳动物物种的 队列研究。
elements_zh.methods: 方法 使用一套综合的计算方法对 马尔堡病毒 (MARV) 基因组 进行多维分子表征。远距离序列同源性通过 BLAST 结合无效模型框架进行询问,并辅以密码子使用偏倚、核苷酸组成和二核苷酸频率的粒度分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果多维分子分析显示 MARV 和哺乳动物群体之间存在不同的基因组相似性,在奇蹄目和某些啮齿动物中观察到多个密码子使用指数的稳定收敛。值得注意的是,马属马 (Equus caballus) 的有效密码子数 (ENC) (52.43) 几乎与 MARV (52.44) 相当,而马马 (Equus asinus) 与病毒的平均 RSCU 曼哈顿距离最低 (0.25)。此外,MARV 的 CpG 抑制 ($$\:{\rho\:}_{CpG}$$ = 0.48) 与所研究的哺乳动物类群的 CpG 消耗水平特征一致。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结论 通过计算生物学的视角,本研究鉴定了奇蹄目和啮齿目中假定的 宿主 队列研究,它们与 MARV 具有不同的基因组、密码子使用和二核苷酸频率同源性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为下游生态场监测、血清流行病学调查和实验验证确立了高度优先的目标,最终为在全球“同一个健康”范式下完善人畜共患 监测 网络提供了科学蓝图。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告研究设计或证据强度评估的具体限制。

papers.title: Narrative review on Marburg virus disease aetiopathogenesis and management
papers.abstract: Abstract On November 14th, 2025, the Ethiopian Ministry of Health confirmed the country’s first Marburg virus outbreak, representing another in a series of recent outbreaks across Africa in only 3 years. Marburg virus disease (MVD) is a highly lethal zoonotic haemorrhagic fever caused by the Marburg virus. This review synthesises the current evidence on MVD, covering epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnostics, and emerging countermeasures, such as investigational antivirals and vaccines. Despite the severity of the disease outcome, no licensed treatment or vaccine exists. Recent outbreaks, including Rwanda (2024), Tanzania and Ethiopia (2025), have accelerated evaluation of investigational therapeutics such as remdesivir and monoclonal antibody MBP091 under expanded access and early‐phase studies; no randomised human efficacy data are currently available for MVD, alongside novel platforms including mRNA and adenovirus-vectored vaccines. Advances in molecular virology have helped to elucidate mechanisms of immune evasion and viral persistence, informing strategies for targeted interventions. Diagnostic capacity and therapeutic deployment remain constrained in resource-limited settings. Strengthening global preparedness will require integrated surveillance, rapid clinical trial frameworks, and equitable access to vaccines and antivirals.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 马尔堡病毒病 (MVD),检查其发病机制和治疗。目标实体包括 马尔堡病毒、马尔堡病以及马尔堡出血热等相关病症。核心问题是综合 MVD 的当前证据,涵盖 流行病学、发病机制、诊断和新兴对策。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 MVD 当前证据的叙述性综合,包括 流行病学、发病机制、诊断和新兴对策。它借鉴了卢旺达(2024 年)、坦桑尼亚和埃塞俄比亚(2025 年)最近的 暴发 的经验,并在扩大使用和早期研究中评估了瑞德西韦和单克隆抗体 MBP091 等研究疗法。目前还没有 MVD 的随机人体功效数据,以及包括 mRNA 和腺病毒载体 疫苗 在内的新型平台。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,马尔堡病毒病 (MVD) 是一种由 马尔堡病毒 引起的高致死性人畜共患出血热。它综合了 MVD 的当前证据,涵盖 流行病学、发病机制、诊断和新兴对策,例如研究性 抗病毒药物 和 疫苗。分子病毒学的进步有助于阐明免疫逃避和病毒持续存在的机制,为有针对性的干预策略提供信息。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 尽管疾病结果很严重,但尚无针对 MVD 的许可 治疗 或 疫苗。在资源有限的环境中,诊断能力和治疗部署仍然受到限制。该审查强调需要通过综合 监测、快速临床试验框架以及公平获取 疫苗 和 抗病毒药物 来加强全球准备。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 加强全球准备需要集成的 监测、快速临床试验框架以及公平获取 疫苗 和 抗病毒药物。该综述强调了进一步研究有效的 治疗 和 疫苗 对于 MVD 的重要性,以及提高资源有限环境中的诊断能力的重要性。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 MVD 当前证据的叙述性综合,包括 流行病学、发病机制、诊断和新兴对策。它借鉴了卢旺达(2024 年)、坦桑尼亚和埃塞俄比亚(2025 年)最近的 暴发 的经验,并在扩大使用和早期研究中评估了瑞德西韦和单克隆抗体 MBP091 等研究疗法。目前还没有 MVD 的随机人体功效数据,以及包括 mRNA 和腺病毒载体 疫苗 在内的新型平台。

analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 加强全球准备需要集成的 监测、快速临床试验框架以及公平获取 疫苗 和 抗病毒药物。该综述强调了进一步研究有效的 治疗 和 疫苗 对于 MVD 的重要性,以及提高资源有限环境中的诊断能力的重要性。

papers.title: A participatory expert-based risk assessment to inform zoonotic disease surveillance in Cameroon: the case of Ebola virus disease and Rift Valley fever
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Viral haemorrhagic fevers (VHFs) are a group of zoonotic diseases caused by RNA viruses, including pathogens such as Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, and Rift Valley fever virus. Previous studies have identified Cameroon as a high-risk country, due to favourable ecoclimatic conditions and the presence of susceptible mammals and vectors that have been confirmed positive for viruses causing Rift Valley fever (RVF) and Ebola virus disease (EVD). Although evidence exists of RVF virus circulation in animals and serological reactivity to Ebola-related viruses among humans in Cameroon, the country has not officially documented epidemics of RVF or EVD. The objective of this study is to provide novel, context-refined knowledge of perceived risk factors and temporal patterns of RVF and EVD emergence in Cameroon, where epidemiological data on these two diseases are limited, with RVF explored through the livestock component and its early transmission dynamics in animal hosts, and zoonotic spillover to humans for EVD. Methods The present work proposes a risk assessment of RVF and EVD emergence through the development of a One Health integrated risk assessment tool for identifying perceived high-risk periods and key risk factors. A mixed, semi-quantitative approach involving expert semi-structured interviews, and a monthly calendar was used for data collection. Expert-based risk evaluation was then compared to risk factors derived from the scientific literature. Results For RVF, the wettest months seem to pose the highest risk, with increased inter-animal transmission during livestock transhumance. Key spatial determinants identified by experts included rainfall, host density, reservoirs, vectors, and livestock movements. For EVD spillover risk, human activities and behaviours, land cover, and host density were also perceived as critical. Convergences and divergences regarding expert-based and literature-based risk factors for RVF and EVD were observed, with variations concerning respectively livestock trade and socio-cultural practices linked to livelihood and forest-based subsistence. The distinction is likely attributable to the differing approaches of contextualization and generalization employed respectively by the two sources of weighting. Conclusions This study shows that, even in regions with no documented disease history, an integrated approach combining expert knowledge and literature-based evidence enables meaningful perceived risk assessment, generates novel and context-specific information, and supports the refinement of preventive strategies. The participatory visual tool introduced allows identification and quantification of putative zoonotic risk factors and their temporal dynamics, informing risk mapping, management, and communication.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limited epidemiological data on Marburg virus and Marburg virus disease in Cameroon, focusing on perceived risk factors and temporal patterns of emergence in a high-risk country with favourable ecoclimatic conditions and susceptible mammals and vectors.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Cameroon, employing a participatory expert-based risk assessment approach to evaluate the emergence of Marburg virus and Marburg virus disease, with a focus on identifying high-risk periods and key risk factors through expert interviews and a monthly calendar.
analysis.methods: A mixed, semi-quantitative method was used, combining expert semi-structured interviews and a monthly calendar to collect data, and comparing expert-based risk evaluations with risk factors derived from the scientific literature.
analysis.main_results: The study found that for Marburg virus, human activities and behaviours, land cover, and host density were perceived as critical risk factors, while for Marburg virus disease, convergences and divergences were observed between expert-based and literature-based risk factors, particularly concerning livestock trade and socio-cultural practices.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that integrating expert knowledge with literature-based evidence provides novel, context-specific insights into perceived risk factors, even in regions without documented disease history, and supports the refinement of preventive strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform zoonotic disease surveillance, risk mapping, and communication strategies in Cameroon, particularly for Marburg virus and its associated disease, by highlighting key risk factors and temporal dynamics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited to expert-based assessments and literature-derived factors, which may introduce bias and lack direct empirical validation, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a participatory expert-based risk assessment to evaluate the emergence of Marburg virus and Marburg virus disease in Cameroon, a high-risk country with favourable conditions for zoonotic diseases. The research aimed to identify perceived risk factors and temporal patterns of these diseases, given the limited epidemiological data. A mixed, semi-quantitative approach was used, combining expert interviews and a monthly calendar to collect data, and comparing these assessments with literature-based risk factors. The results indicated that human activities, land cover, and host density were critical risk factors for Marburg virus, while divergences were observed between expert and literature-based factors for Marburg virus disease, particularly regarding socio-cultural practices. The authors interpreted that integrating expert knowledge with literature provides novel insights for risk assessment and supports the development of targeted preventive strategies. The study's findings can inform surveillance and communication efforts in Cameroon, but the reliance on expert-based data introduces potential biases, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景病毒性出血热(VHF)是一组由RNA病毒引起的人畜共患疾病,包括埃博拉病毒、马尔堡病毒、拉沙病毒和裂谷热病毒等病原体。此前的研究已将喀麦隆确定为高风险国家,原因是其有利的生态气候条件以及易感哺乳动物和 媒介 的存在,这些哺乳动物和 媒介 已被证实对导致裂谷热 (RVF) 和埃博拉病毒病 (EVD) 的病毒呈阳性。尽管有证据表明裂谷热病毒在喀麦隆动物中传播以及人类对埃博拉相关病毒有血清学反应,但该国尚未正式记录裂谷热或埃博拉病毒病的流行情况。本研究的目的是提供关于喀麦隆裂谷热和埃博拉病毒病出现的感知风险因素和时间模式的新颖、具体的知识,喀麦隆关于这两种疾病的流行病学数据有限,通过牲畜成分及其在动物宿主中的早期传播动态和人畜共患埃博拉病毒病中的人畜共患跨物种溢出来探索裂谷热。方法 目前的工作提出通过开发 One Health 综合风险评估工具来识别可感知的高风险期和关键风险因素,对裂谷热和埃博拉病毒病的出现进行风险评估。采用混合、半定量方法,包括专家半结构化访谈和月历来收集数据。然后将基于专家的风险评估与科学文献中得出的风险因素进行比较。结果 对于 RVF,最潮湿的月份似乎风险最高,牲畜转移期间动物间的 传播 增加。专家确定的关键空间决定因素包括降雨量、宿主 密度、储存宿主、媒介 和牲畜迁徙。对于埃博拉病毒病 跨物种溢出 风险,人类活动和行为、土地覆盖和 宿主 密度也被认为至关重要。观察到基于专家和基于文献的裂谷热和埃博拉病毒病风险因素的趋同和分歧,分别与生计和森林生存相关的牲畜贸易和社会文化实践存在差异。这种区别可能归因于两种权重来源分别采用不同的情境化和概括方法。结论 这项研究表明,即使在没有疾病史记录的地区,结合专家知识和文献证据的综合方法也能实现有意义的感知风险评估,生成新颖且针对具体情况的信息,并支持完善预防策略。引入的参与式视觉工具可以识别和量化假定的人畜共患风险因素及其时间动态,为风险绘图、管理和沟通提供信息。

papers.title: The BIOFIRE BioThreat Panel v2.5 demonstrates comparable sensitivity on the FILMARRAY 2.0 and SPOTFIRE systems
papers.abstract: Rapid and sensitive detection of biothreat agents represents a critical capability for first responders, federal agencies, and militaries around the world. For nearly a decade, the BIOFIRE BioThreat Panel v2.5 has been an easy-to use, automated, “lab in a pouch” detection tool utilizing qualitative, multiplexed polymerase chain reaction (PCR) with the BIOFIRE FILMARRAY 2.0 instrument to detect biothreat agents directly from environmental samples in approximately one hour. The BIOFIRE BioThreat Panel v2.5 detects Bacillus anthracis , Brucella melitensis , Burkholderia mallei/pseudomallei , Coxiella burnetii , Francisella tularensis , Rickettsia prowazekii , Yersinia pestis , Eastern equine encephalitis virus, Orthomarburgvirus marburgense , Orthopoxvirus spp., variola virus, Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalitis virus, Orthoebolavirus zairense , and toxin-encoding genes from Clostridium botulinum (botulinum toxin) and Ricinus communis (Ricin toxin). Sensitivity of the BioThreat Panel v2.5 was evaluated on the FILMARRAY 2.0 and SPOTFIRE instruments through side-by-side testing with both platforms. The limit of detection (LoD) for each of the 16 biothreat targets on the panel, including seven bacterial pathogens, seven viral pathogens, and two toxin-encoding genes was determined. The BioThreat Panel v2.5 exhibited equivalent or better sensitivity on SPOTFIRE compared to FILMARRAY 2.0 for all targets, except for Yersinia pestis , which displayed reduced sensitivity due to a modified calling scheme on SPOTFIRE. This study demonstrates that the BioThreat Panel v2.5 can provide sensitive biothreat detection across both BIOFIRE FILMARRAY 2.0 and SPOTFIRE automated PCR instruments.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the sensitivity of the BIOFIRE BioThreat Panel v2.5 for detecting Marburg virus and related pathogens using the FILMARRAY 2.0 and SPOTFIRE systems. The research highlights the importance of rapid and sensitive biothreat detection for first responders and federal agencies. The methods involve qualitative, multiplexed PCR using automated instruments. The main results show that the panel performs equivalently or better on SPOTFIRE compared to FILMARRAY 2.0, except for Yersinia pestis, which had reduced sensitivity due to a modified calling scheme. The interpretation emphasizes the panel's utility for detecting Marburg virus and related agents. The findings have implications for surveillance and diagnosis in field settings. The study does not report limitations or evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 快速、灵敏地检测生物威胁因子是世界各地急救人员、联邦机构和军队的一项关键能力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 近十年来,BIOFIRE BioThreat Panel v2.5 一直是一种易于使用、自动化的“袋装实验室”检测工具,利用定性多重聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 和 BIOFIRE FILMARRAY 2.0 仪器,在大约一小时内直接从环境样本中检测生物威胁物质。
elements_zh.methods: BIOFIRE BioThreat Panel v2.5 可检测 马尔堡病毒、Ravn 病毒和其他病原体,包括来自肉毒杆菌和蓖麻的毒素编码基因。

papers.title_zh: BIOFIRE BioThreat Panel v2.5 在 FILMARRAY 2.0 和 SPOTFIRE 系统上表现出相当的灵敏度
papers.source_body_en: Rapid and sensitive detection of biothreat agents represents a critical capability for first responders, federal agencies, and militaries around the world. For nearly a decade, the BIOFIRE BioThreat Panel v2.5 has been an easy-to use, automated, “lab in a pouch” detection tool utilizing qualitative, multiplexed polymerase chain reaction (PCR) with the BIOFIRE FILMARRAY 2.0 instrument to detect biothreat agents directly from environmental samples in approximately one hour. The BIOFIRE BioThreat Panel v2.5 detects Bacillus anthracis , Brucella melitensis , Burkholderia mallei/pseudomallei , Coxiella burnetii , Francisella tularensis , Rickettsia prowazekii , Yersinia pestis , Eastern equine encephalitis virus, Orthomarburgvirus marburgense , Orthopoxvirus spp., variola virus, Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalitis virus, Orthoebolavirus zairense , and toxin-encoding genes from Clostridium botulinum (botulinum toxin) and Ricinus communis (Ricin toxin). Sensitivity of the BioThreat Panel v2.5 was evaluated on the FILMARRAY 2.0 and SPOTFIRE instruments through side-by-side testing with both platforms. The limit of detection (LoD) for each of the 16 biothreat targets on the panel, including seven bacterial pathogens, seven viral pathogens, and two toxin-encoding genes was determined. The BioThreat Panel v2.5 exhibited equivalent or better sensitivity on SPOTFIRE compared to FILMARRAY 2.0 for all targets, except for Yersinia pestis , which displayed reduced sensitivity due to a modified calling scheme on SPOTFIRE. This study demonstrates that the BioThreat Panel v2.5 can provide sensitive biothreat detection across both BIOFIRE FILMARRAY 2.0 and SPOTFIRE automated PCR instruments.

Committee for Africa in Addis Ababa 4 August 2026 | News Release | Reading time: 3 min Ethiopia to Host the Seventy-sixth Session of the WHO Regional Committee for Africa in Addis Ababa Addis Ababa, Ethiopia | August 2026 – The Government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Office for Africa, will host the Seventy-sixth Session of the WHO Regional Committee for Africa (RC76) in Addis Ababa from 24 to 28 August 2026. The high-level meeting will bring together Ministers of Health and senior officials from the 47 Member States of the WHO African Region, alongside global health leaders, development partners, donors, and representatives from WHO headquarters, the WHO Regional Office for Africa, and WHO country offices. More than 600 delegates are expected to participate in what is the Region's highest annual forum for health governance and policymaking. As the governing body of the WHO Regional Office for Africa, the Regional Committee meets annually to review progress on regional health priorities, adopt policies and strategies, provide oversight of WHO's work in the Region, and set the strategic direction for improving health across Africa. RC76 will provide Africa's foremost platform for high-level policy dialogue and decision-making on the Region's most pressing health priorities. Throughout the five-day session, Member States and partners will review progress, consider regional strategies and resolutions, and agree on collective actions to strengthen health systems, accelerate progress towards universal health coverage, enhance health security, improve emergency preparedness and response, and address emerging public health challenges. The session will also feature technical side events, exhibitions, bilateral meetings and public engagement activities, providing opportunities to showcase innovative health solutions, strengthen partnerships, and promote the exchange of knowledge and experience among countries and institutions. Hosting RC76 underscores Ethiopia's longstanding commitment to advancing public health and regional cooperation. As the diplomatic capital of Africa and home to the African Union and the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), Addis Ababa provides an ideal setting for regional and global leaders to come together to address shared health priorities and advance collective action for better health. The meeting also presents an important opportunity for Ethiopia to showcase progress in strengthening its health system and advancing national health priorities in collaboration with WHO and partners. Recent achievements—including expanded access to essential health services, strengthened health system performance, and the successful containment of the Marburg virus disease outbreak—demonstrate the country's continued commitment to building resilient health systems capable of responding effectively to current and emerging public health challenges. "Hosting the Seventy-sixth Session of the WHO Regional Committee for Africa reflects Ethiopia's strong commitment to regional solidarity and collective action for health," said Professor Francis Chisaka Kasolo, WHO Representative to Ethiopia, the African Union and UNECA. "The meeting will provide an important opportunity for Member States to shape the Region's health agenda, strengthen partnerships, and accelerate progress towards healthier, safer and more resilient communities across Africa." The Government of Ethiopia, together with WHO and its partners, is making extensive preparations to ensure a successful and impactful session that fosters collaboration, advances evidence-informed policymaking, and contributes to improved health outcomes across the African Region. About the WHO Regional Committee for Africa The WHO Regional Committee for Africa is the governing body of the WHO Regional Office for Africa. It comprises Ministers of Health or their representatives from each of the 47 Member States of the WHO African Region. The Committee formulates regional policies, reviews the implementation of WHO's work in the Region, provides oversight of the Regional Office, and guides regional health priorities in accordance with the WHO Constitution and its Rules of Procedure. news.content: Skip to content This page contains press release content distributed by XPR Media. Members of the editorial and news staff of the USA TODAY Network were not involved in the creation of this content. The placement of this content is part of a paid service. Public Health Vaccines (PHV) awarded BioMaP-Consortium contract to onshore manufacturing of its PHV01, rVSV-MARV vaccine Distributed by EIN Presswire PHV to tech transfer production and testing of PHV01 (monovalent VSV ΔG Marburg Angola) to the US to bolster live viral vaccine domestic manufacturing capacity. We’re proud to partner with BioMaP-Consortium, ATI and ABL on this important program, and we thank BioMaP-Consortium/BARDA for their continued commitment and support.” — Dr. Joan Fusco, Chief Operating Officer CAMBRIDGE, MA, UNITED STATES, August 6, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ — Public Health Vaccines, LLC (PHV), a biotechnology company out of Cambridge, MA, has been awarded a contract from the Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing Preparedness Consortium (BioMaP-Consortium) to tech transfer production and testing of its monovalent VSV ΔG Marburg (Angola) vaccine candidate (PHV01) to the United States to bolster live viral vaccine domestic manufacturing capacity. Domestic capacity for producing live viral vectors—particularly those used in viral hemorrhagic fever vaccines—remains limited, and expanding this capability is essential for strengthening the nation’s vaccine manufacturing base, improving health security preparedness, and enabling a faster, more effective response to both known and emerging infectious disease threats. The BioMaP-Consortium brings together pharmaceutical, medical, academic, and scientific organizations working toward successful development and delivery of medical countermeasure materials and products. This project has been funded in whole or in part with federal funds from the Department of Health and Human Services; Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR); Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, under OT number #75A50123D00003. PHV has been developing PHV01 in collaboration with the BARDA since February of 2019 under contract #HHSO100201900022C. Since then, the company has successfully advanced the vaccine candidate through Phase 1 clinical testing and will be entering Phase II clinical testing in the coming months. Under this approximately $11 million award, PHV will transfer the complete PHV01 manufacturing process—including BDS (upstream and downstream) and FDP (formulation, fill/finish)—from offshore facilities to Ascend-ABL’s U.S.-based CGMP manufacturing sites in MD and FL. This transfer will establish domestic readiness for Phase 2-scale production and create a foundation for rapid scale-up during emergencies. PHV’s Chief Operating Officer Dr. Joan Fusco stated, “Robust domestic manufacturing capability is essential to a reliable medical countermeasure supply chain for outbreak preparedness and response. This program is a major step toward establishing the U.S.-based capability and capacity needed to produce recombinant VSV-vectored filovirus vaccines. PHV’s rVSV-Marburg vaccine leads our vaccine portfolio for filoviruses and reflects our successful technology transfers, established manufacturing processes, and platform expertise. We are proud to partner with BioMaP-Consortium, ATI and ABL on this important program to strengthen U.S. outbreak response readiness, and we thank BioMaP-Consortium/BARDA for their continued commitment and support to advance rVSV-based filovirus vaccines.” Marburg virus is a hemorrhagic fever virus of the Filoviridae family that causes Marburg Virus Disease, a rare but severe hemorrhagic fever that affects people and non-human primates and has a fatality ratio of up to 88%. In addition to being a naturally occurring public health threat, it has been determined to present a material threat to national security by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. There are currently no licensed vaccines for Marburg virus; PHV01 will help fill this critical unmet medical need. The PHV01 vaccine is leveraging the proven recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) vector platform originally developed by the Public Health Agency of Canada. About Public Health Vaccines, LLC Public Health Vaccines, LLC. (PHV), headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is a privately-held biotechnology company developing products for the prevention and control of emerging infectious diseases. The company’s primary focus has been on developing vaccines against viral hemorrhagic fevers utilizing the rVSV platform, including multiple vaccines against filoviruses (Marburg virus, Sudan ebolavirus and Ebola Bundibugyo) and a vaccine against the Paramyxovirus, Nipah virus. PHV funding partners for these programs include the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) for its Marburg vaccine, Sudan ebolavirus vaccine and Ebola Bundibugyo vaccine; and the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) for its Nipah vaccine and Ebola Bundibugyo vaccine. For more information, please visit www.phvaccines.com or email info@phvaccines.com. news.title_zh: 公共卫生 疫苗 (PHV) 授予 BioMaP 联盟合同,负责其 PHV01、rVSV-MARV 疫苗 的陆上制造
news.source_body_en: Public Health Vaccines (PHV) has been awarded a contract by the BioMaP-Consortium to transfer the production and testing of its PHV01, rVSV-MARV vaccine to U.S.-based facilities. This move aims to enhance domestic manufacturing capacity for live viral vaccines, particularly for Marburg virus disease, a severe hemorrhagic fever with a high fatality rate. PHV has successfully advanced PHV01 through Phase 1 clinical testing and will enter Phase II testing soon. The vaccine is based on the rVSV platform, originally developed by the Public Health Agency of Canada, and is intended to address the lack of licensed vaccines for Marburg virus. The program is funded by federal agencies, including BARDA, and is part of broader efforts to strengthen the U.S. response to emerging infectious diseases. This development is significant for improving health security and ensuring a reliable supply of medical countermeasures during outbreaks.

news.content_title: Experimental Ebola trial begins in Congo as death toll tops 500
news.content: News City Watch Opinion Lifestyle Sport Entertainment Experimental Ebola trial begins in Congo as death toll tops 500 Bloomberg|Published 1 month ago Ask AI The WHO has announced a new clinical trial of medications to treat ebola more effectively. Image: File Jason Gale and Ashleigh Furlong Patients with the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola have started receiving experimental treatments in a clinical trial that aims to improve care for the rare viral disease, which has killed more than 500 people in Democratic Republic of Congo. The World Health Organization-sponsored trial will test Mapp Biopharmaceutical Inc.’s monoclonal antibody cocktail MBP134 and Gilead Sciences Inc.’s antiviral remdesivir alongside optimized supportive care in Congo’s Ituri province, where the outbreak is concentrated. Designed as an adaptive platform trial, it can continue across future Ebola outbreaks if the current epidemic ends before enough patients are enrolled to produce definitive results. The Partners trial was established with national authorities and scientific partners in record time and “offers real hope that we can deliver concrete results for - and with - the communities at the heart of the outbreak,” WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on social media. “There’s no doubt it’s an extremely challenging situation to run a trial,” said Amanda Rojek, an associate professor of health emergencies at the University of Oxford, which is serving as the trial’s co-ordinating office. While recruitment has just begun, there was a positive reaction from potential patients in the trial, she said. The platform allows researchers to add or remove treatments as evidence emerges, pause enrollment when outbreaks end and restart during future epidemics - allowing evidence to accumulate across outbreaks caused by Ebola viruses and the related Marburg virus until definitive answers are reached. The outbreak has already infected almost 1,600 people in Congo and neighboring Uganda, making it the largest on record caused by Bundibugyo, for which there are no approved vaccines or specific treatments. While the daily number of newly confirmed infections has eased in recent days, transmission remains intense in Ituri, where treatment centers have struggled to keep pace with demand. The trial’s primary endpoint is all-cause mortality 28 days after enrollment. Secondary measures include how quickly patients clear the virus, changes in viral load and organ function, with pregnant women followed through delivery. Researchers aim to recruit several hundred patients over time. Rather than setting a fixed enrollment target for the current epidemic, the protocol allows recruitment to continue across future outbreaks if this one ends before enough participants have been enrolled to answer the study’s central questions. Eligible patients may be randomized independently to receive MBP134, a single-dose monoclonal antibody infusion; remdesivir, given daily for up to 10 days; both therapies; or optimized supportive care alone. Children, pregnant women and breastfeeding women are eligible to participate, reflecting a deliberate effort to include groups historically excluded from outbreak research despite facing some of the highest mortality risks. MBP134 has shown broad activity against multiple Ebola species in laboratory and animal studies, including Bundibugyo, but has only limited experience in humans. Remdesivir, marketed as Veklury, has broad antiviral activity against filoviruses in laboratory testing and extensive safety data from Covid-19, although its benefit against Ebola remains uncertain after earlier studies in Zaire Ebola. WHO is sponsoring the study and Kinshasa-based physician-scientist Placide Mbala Kingebeni is leading it nationally. Researchers don’t know how long it will take for the study to show whether the drugs work. If the drugs are really effective, a solution will be found faster, Rojek said. If the case fatality ratio is low for this subtype of Ebola, then a larger trial might be needed. The speed at which patients are enrolled is also a factor, she said. If a drug is shown to work, the aim is to get it to the wider patient population “as fast as we possibly can,” Rojek added. The study begins as responders contend with mounting challenges beyond the virus itself. Reports from Congo’s National Institute of Public Health in the past week describe attacks on response teams, vandalism of Ebola infrastructure and persistent insecurity disrupting field operations. An infection-prevention team was attacked and its vehicle stoned during decontamination work in North Kivu over the weekend. Health authorities also continue to report gaps in contact tracing, community resistance to screening and treatment, and overcrowded Ebola treatment centers. Even so, the response is expanding. New diagnostic laboratories have opened closer to transmission hotspots, additional treatment capacity is under construction and authorities have begun offering free health-care in several of the hardest-hit areas to encourage patients to seek care earlier. “The real challenge is always for us safety of our team and safety for our patients,” said Rojek. | Bloomberg Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information Opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information We won't sell or share your personal information to inform the ads you see. 06.08.2026 Ebola Outbreak: What You Need to Know Project HOPE is monitoring the Ebola outbreak and connecting local partners with medical supplies. The team previously responded to the outbreak in Uganda and worked with local partners to strengthen outbreak response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Learn more about our response. By Emma Schwartz The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda are confronting the third largest Ebola outbreak in recorded human history. On May 15, 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared the outbreak a “public health emergency of international concern” following cross-border transmission into Uganda. The number of suspected and confirmed cases continues to rise, with much of the outbreak occurring in the DRC’s northeastern areas. In Uganda, Project HOPE has trained health workers, supported contact tracing efforts, and worked closely with government officials to prevent further spread. In the DRC, we have worked with local partners to distribute critical supplies. Read on to learn more about our response. >> Read our latest situation report What You Need to Know: There have been at least 2,444 confirmed cases of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola virus and 969 confirmed deaths across the DRC and Uganda. A backlog of suspected cases still under investigation in the DRC, and women currently make up the majority of suspected cases. Ebola disease is a severe and often life-threatening illness that can spread quickly and carries a high fatality rate. What is happening in Central and East Africa? Families in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda are facing a deadly Ebola outbreak. The outbreak was officially declared by the DRC’s Ministry of Public Health, Hygiene and Social Welfare on May 15, 2026, with cases first identified in the northeastern province of Ituri. Since then, infections have spread across multiple provinces, placing communities and already strained health systems under increasing pressure. This is the DRC’s 17th outbreak of Ebola since the virus was first identified in 1976. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, a rare form of the virus. There is currently no preventative vaccine or treatment for this specific strain, which health officials estimate carries a 30% to 40% fatality rate. The region is already affected by conflict, displacement, food insecurity, and limited access to healthcare, which will make it more difficult to detect cases, trace contacts, and stop the virus from spreading. Cases linked to the outbreak have been confirmed in neighboring Uganda, where health authorities are working to increase the capacity of health workers and identify suspected cases. Team members from African Initiative for Relief and Development (AIRD) distribute personal protective equipment (PPE) in 2025 in response to an Ebola outbreak in Kasai Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, with support provided by Project HOPE. Project HOPE is on the ground responding to the current Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. All photos courtesy AIRD, 2025. Used with permission. Why is the risk growing? Although official borders between the DRC and Uganda are closed except for humanitarian personnel and aid deliveries, unofficial border crossings continue. In addition, Ebola’s long incubation period — which can last up to 21 days — and the similarity of the disease’s symptoms to malaria, makes it difficult to identify and leads to delays in detection and treatment. The outbreak poses a significant risk to frontline health workers and caregivers treating ill patients and family members, creating widespread fear and the potential for devastating burnout. Limited personal protective equipment (PPE) and infection prevention and control (IPC) supplies are making it increasingly difficult to safely provide basic health services. At the same time, gaps in access to healthcare may force sick patients to travel further from home in search of treatment, increasing the risk of spread. Community resistance to recognizing the disease and how it spreads also present major challenges to addressing, controlling, and ending the outbreak. Experts also note that the complex humanitarian situation in northeastern DRC, where non-state actors oversee both remote communities and important urban centers like Goma, is complicating contact tracing and broader containment efforts. >> News Alert: Mobilizing Response to Ebola Outbreak in the DRC & Uganda What is Ebola? Ebola disease is a severe and often life-threatening illness caused by viruses in the filoviridae family. Although relatively rare, Ebola can spread quickly and place significant strain on health systems and communities. Ebola is most prevalent in Central and East Africa as the virus’s natural reservoir is believed to be fruit bats that live in tropical forest ecosystems found across the region. Human outbreaks typically begin when people come into contact with infected wildlife, such as bats or other animals that have contracted the virus. Ebola spreads through direct contact with blood, bodily fluids, or tissues of an infected person, as well as contaminated objects such as bedding, clothing, or medical equipment. Once introduced into a community, Ebola can spread rapidly. Early detection, isolation, supportive care, and vaccination are critical to controlling outbreaks and reducing mortality. Team members from AIRD mobilize PPE for health workers in 2025. Once introduced into a community, Ebola can spread rapidly, making early detection, isolation, supportive care, and vaccination critical to reducing mortality. What is Project HOPE’s response? Project HOPE’s Emergency Response Team continues to monitor the situation and is actively looking to support local partners with medical supplies. We previously responded to the outbreak in Uganda and worked with local partners to strengthen response capacity in both countries. In coordination with Ugandan officials, Project HOPE strengthened surveillance and contact tracing efforts to help detect and contain potential cases. Although case numbers in Uganda remain relatively low, there is an opportunity to improve surveillance practices in at-risk health facilities in the capital of Kampala and in health districts bordering the DRC. Project HOPE also partnered with African Initiative for Relief and Development (AIRD) to rapidly deliver PPE to frontline responders. Working closely with local health officials, partners, and suppliers, we distributed critical PPE and IPC materials in the DRC, including gloves, face masks, and biohazard equipment. In addition, our teams provided tailored technical training and skills reinforcement for frontline responders, with a focus on surveillance and contact tracing, IPC, and mental health and resilience. Across all activities for this response, Project HOPE has worked to ensure that those best positioned to prevent and stop the spread of Ebola have the tools they need to do so. >> READ MORE: We’ve Seen an Ebola Crisis Before. We Cannot Repeat the Same Mistakes. What is Project HOPE’s history of outbreak response in the region? Project HOPE has engaged in outbreak response activities across the African continent, including a response to the 2025 Zaire strain Ebola outbreak in the DRC’s Kasai Province and a successful intervention earlier this year that helped eradicate the Marburg virus in Ethiopia. Project HOPE also responded to the 2014 West African Ebola outbreak in Sierra Leone, providing medicines, medical supplies, and medical consumables such as PPE. Do one thing today. analysis.brief_en: Project HOPE is monitoring the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, which was declared a public health emergency of international concern on May 15, 2026, by the World Health Organization (WHO). The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has resulted in at least 2,444 confirmed cases and 969 confirmed deaths, with much of the spread occurring in the DRC’s northeastern areas. Women make up the majority of suspected cases, and the outbreak is the third largest in recorded history. The Bundibugyo strain has a 30% to 40% fatality rate, and there is currently no preventative vaccine or treatment. Project HOPE is working with local partners to distribute critical supplies, train health workers, and support contact tracing efforts in both countries. However, challenges persist due to limited personal protective equipment (PPE) and infection prevention and control (IPC) supplies, as well as community resistance to recognizing the disease and its transmission. The outbreak is also complicated by the region’s existing humanitarian crises, including conflict, displacement, and food insecurity, which hinder containment efforts.

Island Pharmaceuticals (ASX:ILA) has disclosed details of its dual approach to advancing galidesivir as a broad-acting antiviral targeting multiple filovirus threats, including confirmation from the FDA that the Animal Rule pathway is appropriate for developing countermeasures against Marburg virus, and that galidesivir would qualify for a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher upon approval. Key Points FDA confirmed the Animal Rule pathway is appropriate for galidesivir as a Marburg virus countermeasure and provided clear guidance on clinical program design FDA advised galidesivir would qualify for a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher on approval; the most recent PRV sold for US$200 million Galidesivir has demonstrated multi-filovirus activity across Marburg, Ebola and Sudan strains, with 94% survival in a Marburg non-human primate model with treatment initiated up to 48 hours post-infection The company reported cash at bank of $12.87 million as at 30 June 2026, with no debt and potential additional capital of approximately $3.2 million from vested options where the current share price exceeds the exercise price Island intends to commence the next galidesivir animal study in Marburg imminently, based on FDA feedback Filovirus Threat Landscape and Preparedness Gap According to the filing, the United States lacks a broad-acting antiviral capable of addressing multiple filovirus threats. Existing Ebola countermeasures are strain-specific to Zaire only, and there are no approved therapeutics for Marburg, Bundibugyo or Sudan virus. The filing states that fatality rates are extremely high, with Marburg up to 88%, Ebola up to 90%, Sudan up to 47%, and Bundibugyo between 30% and 50%. The filing also notes that an ongoing Bundibugyo outbreak has no available medical countermeasures, and that the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak surpassed the 2018–2020 Ebola Zaire total in approximately 70 days. Galidesivir Efficacy Data and Regulatory Pathway The filing states that galidesivir has demonstrated 94% survival in a Marburg non-human primate model with treatment initiated up to 48 hours post-infection. In an Ebola Zaire Kikwit non-human primate model, the filing discloses 100% survival when treatment commenced two days post-infection, and 67% survival when treatment commenced three days post-infection. The compound has both intravenous and intramuscular formulations with a reported favourable safety profile. The filing also states that galidesivir's manufacturing route has been improved with a two-to-three times yield increase, and that development has been supported by NIAID and BARDA with more than US$70 million historically. Strategic National Stockpile Opportunity and Company Overview The filing notes that since 2012, the FDA's Animal Rule approval has led to eight bioterror countermeasures joining the US Strategic National Stockpile, with seven of the eight continuing under SNS contract and generating lifetime sales of between US$100 million and US$1.2 billion, at an average of US$467 million. The filing states that Marburg is the only Category A biothreat with no treatment currently available in the Strategic National Stockpile. As at 6 August 2026, Island Pharmaceuticals had 295,916,682 shares on issue at $0.445 per share, representing a market capitalisation of $131.68 million. Confirmation Aditi Sarkar Aditi Sarkar brings over two years of experience in equity-focused research and secondary analysis, underpinned by a strong academic foundation. She joined the Kalkine team in April 2024 and holds a postgraduate degree in life sciences. 07 August 2026 01:17 PM AEST Share X (Formerly Twitter) Whatsapp Facebook LinkedIn Telegram Email This Article Copy Link ‹ ILA | AUD 0.45 › Summarize with AI Chat GPT Perplexity Start Your Free Trial Now! Island Pharmaceuticals (ASX:ILA) has disclosed details of its dual approach to advancing galidesivir as a broad-acting antiviral targeting multiple filovirus threats, including confirmation from the FDA that the Animal Rule pathway is appropriate for developing countermeasures against Marburg virus, and that galidesivir would qualify for a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher upon approval. Key Points FDA confirmed the Animal Rule pathway is appropriate for galidesivir as a Marburg virus countermeasure and provided clear guidance on clinical program design FDA advised galidesivir would qualify for a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher on approval; the most recent PRV sold for US$200 million Galidesivir has demonstrated multi-filovirus activity across Marburg, Ebola and Sudan strains, with 94% survival in a Marburg non-human primate model with treatment initiated up to 48 hours post-infection The company reported cash at bank of $12.87 million as at 30 June 2026, with no debt and potential additional capital of approximately $3.2 million from vested options where the current share price exceeds the exercise price Island intends to commence the next galidesivir animal study in Marburg imminently, based on FDA feedback Filovirus Threat Landscape and Preparedness Gap According to the filing, the United States lacks a broad-acting antiviral capable of addressing multiple filovirus threats. Existing Ebola countermeasures are strain-specific to Zaire only, and there are no approved therapeutics for Marburg, Bundibugyo or Sudan virus. The filing states that fatality rates are extremely high, with Marburg up to 88%, Ebola up to 90%, Sudan up to 47%, and Bundibugyo between 30% and 50%. The filing also notes that an ongoing Bundibugyo outbreak has no available medical countermeasures, and that the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak surpassed the 2018–2020 Ebola Zaire total in approximately 70 days. Galidesivir Efficacy Data and Regulatory Pathway The filing states that galidesivir has demonstrated 94% survival in a Marburg non-human primate model with treatment initiated up to 48 hours post-infection. In an Ebola Zaire Kikwit non-human primate model, the filing discloses 100% survival when treatment commenced two days post-infection, and 67% survival when treatment commenced three days post-infection. The compound has both intravenous and intramuscular formulations with a reported favourable safety profile. The filing also states that galidesivir's manufacturing route has been improved with a two-to-three times yield increase, and that development has been supported by NIAID and BARDA with more than US$70 million historically. Strategic National Stockpile Opportunity and Company Overview The filing notes that since 2012, the FDA's Animal Rule approval has led to eight bioterror countermeasures joining the US Strategic National Stockpile, with seven of the eight continuing under SNS contract and generating lifetime sales of between US$100 million and US$1.2 billion, at an average of US$467 million. The filing states that Marburg is the only Category A biothreat with no treatment currently available in the Strategic National Stockpile. As at 6 August 2026, Island Pharmaceuticals had 295,916,682 shares on issue at $0.445 per share, representing a market capitalisation of $131.68 million. news.title_zh: Island Pharmaceuticals 推进 Galidesivir 作为 Pan-丝状病毒 医疗对策,并获得 FDA 动物规则确认 - Kalkine
news.source_body_en: Island Pharmaceuticals has received FDA confirmation that the Animal Rule pathway is appropriate for developing galidesivir as a countermeasure against Marburg virus, and that the drug would qualify for a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher upon approval. The FDA also provided guidance on the clinical program design for galidesivir. The company reported that galidesivir has demonstrated 94% survival in a Marburg non-human primate model when treatment is initiated up to 48 hours post-infection. This is significant as Marburg is the only Category A biothreat with no treatment currently available in the Strategic National Stockpile. The filing highlights that existing Ebola countermeasures are strain-specific to Zaire only, and there are no approved therapeutics for Marburg, Bundibugyo, or Sudan virus. Island Pharmaceuticals plans to start the next animal study for galidesivir in Marburg soon, based on FDA feedback. The company has a reported cash at bank of $12.87 million as of 30 June 2026, with no debt and potential additional capital of approximately $3.2 million from vested options. The development of galidesivir has been supported by NIAID and BARDA with more than $70 million historically.

Public Health Vaccines (PHV) awarded BioMaP-Consortium contract to onshore manufacturing of its PHV01, rVSV-MARV vaccine News Provided By Public Health Vaccines August 06, 2026, 13:00 GMT Share This Article PHV to tech transfer production and testing of PHV01 (monovalent VSV ΔG Marburg Angola) to the US to bolster live viral vaccine domestic manufacturing capacity. We're proud to partner with BioMaP-Consortium, ATI and ABL on this important program, and we thank BioMaP-Consortium/BARDA for their continued commitment and support.” — Dr. Joan Fusco, Chief Operating Officer CAMBRIDGE, MA, UNITED STATES, August 6, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- Public Health Vaccines, LLC (PHV), a biotechnology company out of Cambridge, MA, has been awarded a contract from the Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing Preparedness Consortium (BioMaP-Consortium) to tech transfer production and testing of its monovalent VSV ΔG Marburg (Angola) vaccine candidate (PHV01) to the United States to bolster live viral vaccine domestic manufacturing capacity. Domestic capacity for producing live viral vectors—particularly those used in viral hemorrhagic fever vaccines—remains limited, and expanding this capability is essential for strengthening the nation’s vaccine manufacturing base, improving health security preparedness, and enabling a faster, more effective response to both known and emerging infectious disease threats. The BioMaP-Consortium brings together pharmaceutical, medical, academic, and scientific organizations working toward successful development and delivery of medical countermeasure materials and products. This project has been funded in whole or in part with federal funds from the Department of Health and Human Services; Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR); Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, under OT number #75A50123D00003. PHV has been developing PHV01 in collaboration with the BARDA since February of 2019 under contract #HHSO100201900022C. Since then, the company has successfully advanced the vaccine candidate through Phase 1 clinical testing and will be entering Phase II clinical testing in the coming months. Under this approximately $11 million award, PHV will transfer the complete PHV01 manufacturing process—including BDS (upstream and downstream) and FDP (formulation, fill/finish)—from offshore facilities to Ascend-ABL’s U.S.-based CGMP manufacturing sites in MD and FL. This transfer will establish domestic readiness for Phase 2-scale production and create a foundation for rapid scale-up during emergencies. PHV’s Chief Operating Officer Dr. Joan Fusco stated, “Robust domestic manufacturing capability is essential to a reliable medical countermeasure supply chain for outbreak preparedness and response. This program is a major step toward establishing the U.S.-based capability and capacity needed to produce recombinant VSV-vectored filovirus vaccines. PHV’s rVSV-Marburg vaccine leads our vaccine portfolio for filoviruses and reflects our successful technology transfers, established manufacturing processes, and platform expertise. We are proud to partner with BioMaP-Consortium, ATI and ABL on this important program to strengthen U.S. outbreak response readiness, and we thank BioMaP-Consortium/BARDA for their continued commitment and support to advance rVSV-based filovirus vaccines.” Marburg virus is a hemorrhagic fever virus of the Filoviridae family that causes Marburg Virus Disease, a rare but severe hemorrhagic fever that affects people and non-human primates and has a fatality ratio of up to 88%. In addition to being a naturally occurring public health threat, it has been determined to present a material threat to national security by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. There are currently no licensed vaccines for Marburg virus; PHV01 will help fill this critical unmet medical need. The PHV01 vaccine is leveraging the proven recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) vector platform originally developed by the Public Health Agency of Canada. About Public Health Vaccines, LLC Public Health Vaccines, LLC. (PHV), headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is a privately-held biotechnology company developing products for the prevention and control of emerging infectious diseases. The company’s primary focus has been on developing vaccines against viral hemorrhagic fevers utilizing the rVSV platform, including multiple vaccines against filoviruses (Marburg virus, Sudan ebolavirus and Ebola Bundibugyo) and a vaccine against the Paramyxovirus, Nipah virus. PHV funding partners for these programs include the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) for its Marburg vaccine, Sudan ebolavirus vaccine and Ebola Bundibugyo vaccine; and the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) for its Nipah vaccine and Ebola Bundibugyo vaccine. Public Health Vaccines (PHV) awarded BioMaP-Consortium contract to onshore manufacturing of its PHV01, rVSV-MARV vaccine News Provided By Public Health Vaccines August 06, 2026, 13:00 GMT Share This Article PHV to tech transfer production and testing of PHV01 (monovalent VSV ΔG Marburg Angola) to the US to bolster live viral vaccine domestic manufacturing capacity. We're proud to partner with BioMaP-Consortium, ATI and ABL on this important program, and we thank BioMaP-Consortium/BARDA for their continued commitment and support.” — Dr. Joan Fusco, Chief Operating Officer CAMBRIDGE, MA, UNITED STATES, August 6, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- Public Health Vaccines, LLC (PHV), a biotechnology company out of Cambridge, MA, has been awarded a contract from the Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing Preparedness Consortium (BioMaP-Consortium) to tech transfer production and testing of its monovalent VSV ΔG Marburg (Angola) vaccine candidate (PHV01) to the United States to bolster live viral vaccine domestic manufacturing capacity. Domestic capacity for producing live viral vectors—particularly those used in viral hemorrhagic fever vaccines—remains limited, and expanding this capability is essential for strengthening the nation’s vaccine manufacturing base, improving health security preparedness, and enabling a faster, more effective response to both known and emerging infectious disease threats. The BioMaP-Consortium brings together pharmaceutical, medical, academic, and scientific organizations working toward successful development and delivery of medical countermeasure materials and products. This project has been funded in whole or in part with federal funds from the Department of Health and Human Services; Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR); Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, under OT number #75A50123D00003. PHV has been developing PHV01 in collaboration with the BARDA since February of 2019 under contract #HHSO100201900022C. Since then, the company has successfully advanced the vaccine candidate through Phase 1 clinical testing and will be entering Phase II clinical testing in the coming months. Under this approximately $11 million award, PHV will transfer the complete PHV01 manufacturing process—including BDS (upstream and downstream) and FDP (formulation, fill/finish)—from offshore facilities to Ascend-ABL’s U.S.-based CGMP manufacturing sites in MD and FL. This transfer will establish domestic readiness for Phase 2-scale production and create a foundation for rapid scale-up during emergencies. PHV’s Chief Operating Officer Dr. Joan Fusco stated, “Robust domestic manufacturing capability is essential to a reliable medical countermeasure supply chain for outbreak preparedness and response. This program is a major step toward establishing the U.S.-based capability and capacity needed to produce recombinant VSV-vectored filovirus vaccines. PHV’s rVSV-Marburg vaccine leads our vaccine portfolio for filoviruses and reflects our successful technology transfers, established manufacturing processes, and platform expertise. We are proud to partner with BioMaP-Consortium, ATI and ABL on this important program to strengthen U.S. outbreak response readiness, and we thank BioMaP-Consortium/BARDA for their continued commitment and support to advance rVSV-based filovirus vaccines.” Marburg virus is a hemorrhagic fever virus of the Filoviridae family that causes Marburg Virus Disease, a rare but severe hemorrhagic fever that affects people and non-human primates and has a fatality ratio of up to 88%. In addition to being a naturally occurring public health threat, it has been determined to present a material threat to national security by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. There are currently no licensed vaccines for Marburg virus; PHV01 will help fill this critical unmet medical need. The PHV01 vaccine is leveraging the proven recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) vector platform originally developed by the Public Health Agency of Canada. About Public Health Vaccines, LLC Public Health Vaccines, LLC. (PHV), headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is a privately-held biotechnology company developing products for the prevention and control of emerging infectious diseases. The company’s primary focus has been on developing vaccines against viral hemorrhagic fevers utilizing the rVSV platform, including multiple vaccines against filoviruses (Marburg virus, Sudan ebolavirus and Ebola Bundibugyo) and a vaccine against the Paramyxovirus, Nipah virus. PHV funding partners for these programs include the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) for its Marburg vaccine, Sudan ebolavirus vaccine and Ebola Bundibugyo vaccine; and the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) for its Nipah vaccine and Ebola Bundibugyo vaccine. For more information, please visit www.phvaccines.com or email info@phvaccines.com. Send a FREE Release ↓ Public Health Vaccines (PHV) awarded BioMaP-Consortium contract to onshore manufacturing of its PHV01, rVSV-MARV vaccine News Provided By Public Health Vaccines August 06, 2026, 13:00 GMT Share This Article PHV to tech transfer production and testing of PHV01 (monovalent VSV ΔG Marburg Angola) to the US to bolster live viral vaccine domestic manufacturing capacity. We're proud to partner with BioMaP-Consortium, ATI and ABL on this important program, and we thank BioMaP-Consortium/BARDA for their continued commitment and support.” — Dr. Joan Fusco, Chief Operating Officer CAMBRIDGE, MA, UNITED STATES, August 6, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- Public Health Vaccines, LLC (PHV), a biotechnology company out of Cambridge, MA, has been awarded a contract from the Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing Preparedness Consortium (BioMaP-Consortium) to tech transfer production and testing of its monovalent VSV ΔG Marburg (Angola) vaccine candidate (PHV01) to the United States to bolster live viral vaccine domestic manufacturing capacity. Domestic capacity for producing live viral vectors—particularly those used in viral hemorrhagic fever vaccines—remains limited, and expanding this capability is essential for strengthening the nation’s vaccine manufacturing base, improving health security preparedness, and enabling a faster, more effective response to both known and emerging infectious disease threats. The BioMaP-Consortium brings together pharmaceutical, medical, academic, and scientific organizations working toward successful development and delivery of medical countermeasure materials and products. This project has been funded in whole or in part with federal funds from the Department of Health and Human Services; Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR); Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, under OT number #75A50123D00003. PHV has been developing PHV01 in collaboration with the BARDA since February of 2019 under contract #HHSO100201900022C. Since then, the company has successfully advanced the vaccine candidate through Phase 1 clinical testing and will be entering Phase II clinical testing in the coming months. Under this approximately $11 million award, PHV will transfer the complete PHV01 manufacturing process—including BDS (upstream and downstream) and FDP (formulation, fill/finish)—from offshore facilities to Ascend-ABL’s U.S.-based CGMP manufacturing sites in MD and FL. This transfer will establish domestic readiness for Phase 2-scale production and create a foundation for rapid scale-up during emergencies. PHV’s Chief Operating Officer Dr. Joan Fusco stated, “Robust domestic manufacturing capability is essential to a reliable medical countermeasure supply chain for outbreak preparedness and response. This program is a major step toward establishing the U.S.-based capability and capacity needed to produce recombinant VSV-vectored filovirus vaccines. PHV’s rVSV-Marburg vaccine leads our vaccine portfolio for filoviruses and reflects our successful technology transfers, established manufacturing processes, and platform expertise. We are proud to partner with BioMaP-Consortium, ATI and ABL on this important program to strengthen U.S. outbreak response readiness, and we thank BioMaP-Consortium/BARDA for their continued commitment and support to advance rVSV-based filovirus vaccines.” Marburg virus is a hemorrhagic fever virus of the Filoviridae family that causes Marburg Virus Disease, a rare but severe hemorrhagic fever that affects people and non-human primates and has a fatality ratio of up to 88%. In addition to being a naturally occurring public health threat, it has been determined to present a material threat to national security by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security. There are currently no licensed vaccines for Marburg virus; PHV01 will help fill this critical unmet medical need. The PHV01 vaccine is leveraging the proven recombinant vesicular stomatitis virus (rVSV) vector platform originally developed by the Public Health Agency of Canada. About Public Health Vaccines, LLC Public Health Vaccines, LLC. (PHV), headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is a privately-held biotechnology company developing products for the prevention and control of emerging infectious diseases. The company’s primary focus has been on developing vaccines against viral hemorrhagic fevers utilizing the rVSV platform, including multiple vaccines against filoviruses (Marburg virus, Sudan ebolavirus and Ebola Bundibugyo) and a vaccine against the Paramyxovirus, Nipah virus. PHV funding partners for these programs include the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) for its Marburg vaccine, Sudan ebolavirus vaccine and Ebola Bundibugyo vaccine; and the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) for its Nipah vaccine and Ebola Bundibugyo vaccine. For more information, please visit www.phvaccines.com or email info@phvaccines.com.
